extracted.intended_audience: researchers and scientists who use PubPeer (commenters and authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Platform-specific guidelines for writing, posting, and moderating post-publication comments on scholarly publications (PubPeer). Focuses on required evidence, tone, formatting, moderation thresholds, anonymity and author reply rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication eligibility / recognized ID required
rubrics_metrics.description: What publications can be discussed? Any publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only requirement is for the publication to have an ID that we recognize. Such IDs include the DOI and IDs for PubMed and the ArXiv. Note that failure of searches for DOIs often reflect problems with indexing by the journal or CrossRef.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted classes of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: What classes of comments can I make? Major, minor, negative or positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PubPeer accepts all types of comments about papers. Although many comments concern issues that are central to a paper’s conclusions, this is not an obligation. Comments about minor issues and details should be interpreted as such, although attention to detail is often important. The site may draw the line at issues that have no significant bearing on the science, its interpretation or its presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirement — facts, logic and publicly verifiable information
rubrics_metrics.description: What can my comment contain? Facts, logic and publicly verifiable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base statements on publicly verifiable information (data in the paper, another paper, book, newspaper, website). Include supporting information in the comment and at least cite your sources. This allows easy verification of the comment's quality. Imagine having to defend the truth of your statement in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearsay and personal-knowledge prohibition (anonymous-highbar exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments based upon hearsay are unacceptable — e.g., 'My friend used to work in the lab and said their glassware is dirty'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports of personal knowledge must be made using a signed account and supported as strongly as possible; they will be moderated case-by-case. This means PubPeer is not particularly suitable for whistleblowers whose comments are based upon personal knowledge unless they sign and strongly support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations of misconduct rule / high moderation bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of misconduct are forbidden on PubPeer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separately, comments implying potential misconduct are subject to a high moderation bar. Moderators evaluate such comments by asking themselves, 'would we be happy to run a truth defence in a defamation case?'. If you make such implications, be prepared to provide very strong, publicly verifiable evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal comments and speculation about motives
rubrics_metrics.description: You should avoid personal comments about authors and speculation about researcher actions and motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal and speculative remarks are non-scientific and can pose legal problems. Focus on factual and logical issues rather than character or intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: polite, neutral and factual; avoid hyperbole
rubrics_metrics.description: What tone should I adopt? Polite, neutral and factual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessarily strong language and hyperbolic adjectives (examples given: 'critical', 'crucial', 'fundamental', 'major', 'glaring', 'blatant', 'severe', 'profound', 'catastrophic', 'devastating', 'highly', 'massive', 'deeply', 'fatal', 'catergorically', 'paramount'...). A good approach is to imagine writing a careful scientific paper rather than shouting on social media. Also avoid speechifying about 'rigour', 'scientific integrity' and the 'scientific record'.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality comment features: specificity, analysis, support and context
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write a high-quality comment? Specificity, analysis, support and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish within the comment the issues you wish to discuss, typically by identifying and including the figures, tables, quotes, equations that you will discuss. Avoid unfocused language; demonstrate your conclusion rather than just stating it. Provide context so the comment is useful to other readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and formatting (Markdown/preview/editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof-read your comment carefully before posting; comments are formatted using Markdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the preview pane provided. Careless writing creates a poor impression. Comments can be edited after submission until accepted or another comment is submitted in the same thread (and editing rules differ for whitelisted/greylisted users).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include explanation as text (not embedded in images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include your explanation as text in the comment rather than including it within an image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators can perform minor editing on text to make comments acceptable (e.g., removing explicit allegations) but cannot edit text embedded within images; comments relying on image-embedded text may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting information requirement and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting information should be provided, in the comment if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data, marked-up images, calculations, or links to datasets/repositories. If suggesting serious plagiarism, show sufficient textual analysis with copy and source shown side-by-side and marked up. Larger datasets should be submitted to specialist providers (Dryad, Zenodo, figshare) and linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image-evidence standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If highlighting suspected image irregularities, provide marked-up images to prove your assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure uploaded images have sufficient size and resolution for the site's zoom feature. If you believe a particular transformation underlies an irregularity, perform the transformation yourself and include the result. Check for innocent explanations (gel reprobes, shared loading controls, adjacent tissue regions). Comments highlighting compression artefacts will be rejected. The output from automatic image analysis tools (e.g., Error Level Analysis) is almost never interpreted correctly; such analyses are usually rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image duplication: check for innocent experimental explanations first
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe image parts have been (inadvertently) duplicated, check whether experimental design offers an innocent explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for gel reprobes, cases where panels share loading controls, or neighbouring tissue regions that naturally overlap. Overlaps can be innocent; unannounced elision of whole lanes from a gel is not considered a concern except in recent articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical improbability — provide calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe results are numerically improbable (or impossible), provide a calculation demonstrating this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may accept obvious cases without calculations, but providing a calculation strengthens the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a homework site — show prior effort
rubrics_metrics.description: This is not a homework site. Requests for explanation can be acceptable, but you should provide evidence of having tried to understand the relevant sections and cited literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PubPeer prefers comments that provide expert insight over those that display ignorance. Demonstrate understanding and the significance of the issue raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism of analysis/modeling must be substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of specific analysis and modelling methods should explain why they are unreasonable/erroneous and significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with the purpose, design and methods of the article. Appending a brain-dump to a random quotation is insufficient. For Bayesian analyses, criticism solely for using Bayesian statistics is not considered useful; substantive discussion of priors is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion-of-limitations must link to influence on conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of limitations should be linked to an analysis of their influence on the results/conclusions of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that merely point out limitations without connecting them to the article's conclusions are likely to be rejected. Requests for a different paper are (very) likely to be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and contribution: avoid comments that add nothing new
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments adding nothing (or nothing new) to the scientific discussion, particularly anonymous comments merely supporting another comment or voicing an opinion, are not suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to add substantive, verifiable content rather than mere agreement or unsupported opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-scientific commentary discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-scientific commentary should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on factual and logical issues related to the research rather than political, promotional, or purely personal commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: General comments and coordinated campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: General comments should be carefully linked to the specific article; the site may limit campaigns making such comments on many papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More leeway is given for reviews, discussion papers and editorials. Moderators may limit broadly repeated general comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrelevant citations: require clear demonstration of irrelevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments highlighting irrelevant citations should ideally focus on egregious cases or explain the irrelevance clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may lack domain knowledge; they will only accept cases where there is no possible ambiguity about what the citation was intended to support. Often the citation context is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement/author-ads rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments displaying paper/authorship advertisements need to include an image AND a link to a publicly verifiable datestamped archive of the advertisement predating publication of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is challenging because many social media prevent archival by services like the Internet Archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I post external links? Please do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to other articles, blog posts, newspaper articles, and relevant information are encouraged. However, indiscriminate bulk linking campaigns are discouraged and may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation powers and process
rubrics_metrics.description: How does moderation work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PubPeer reserves the right to remove or edit comments that do not conform to guidelines. Report non-conforming comments using the 'report' button. Anonymous and greylisted accounts' comments only appear after moderation (can take up to a week). Moderation is based on content, not identity; no user- or author-specific blocks are operated, though users can be greylisted or whitelisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance threshold for allegations and legal defensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators assess comments for legal risk with an eye to defamation defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To defend defamation cases PubPeer may have to prove the truth of statements; authors/commenters should make it easy to evaluate legal risk by carefully supporting statements and logic, ideally within the comment itself. If you can't afford to defend yourself, you lose.

rubrics_metrics.name: PubPeer does not review comments scientifically — reader responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer does not review comments scientifically and provides no warranty as to their veracity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All readers should evaluate comments for themselves. PubPeer complements pre-publication review rather than reproducing it, and it lacks resources to implement scientific review or access original data in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author alerts and reply capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do authors receive alerts? Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are automatically alerted when their paper is commented. Author replies must use a signed account validated via a plausible institutional email address. Many questions can be resolved by showing original data; authors are encouraged to post data publicly. PubPeer will not normally remove comments merely because authors reply or journals publish corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and account rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How can I ensure anonymity? Use Tor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PubPeer minimizes user information; users seeking strongest anonymity should use Tor. Anonymous access codes cannot be recovered if lost (create new account). Pseudonyms are assigned randomly from the tree of life; users cannot choose their own pseudonym. New pseudonym accounts are greylisted and comments require moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and takedown policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I claim a copyright violation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PubPeer provides a procedure for copyright notifications and will oppose unfounded takedown notices. Reproduction of figures and text for the purpose of 'criticism' is considered fair use under US law (where PubPeer is incorporated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of obvious errors, unclear comments, conspiracy and disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that are obviously erroneous or unclear will be rejected; conspiracy theories and disinformation will be blocked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may reject comments, especially in the context of seemingly malicious or misguided serial posts. The site aims to keep discussion factual and useful.
